dtype.evidence: User decision (2026-10-09): the reference-dtype GGUF comes from the deployed whistle.cact, not the F32 QAT-master safetensors. whistle.cact stores 152 matmul weights as Cactus Quants CQ (145 x 2-bit, 7 x 4-bit: embedding + mHC; group 128; w_group = (codebook[idx] * group_norm) @ normalized Walsh-Hadamard(128)), 524 tensors FP16, 4 FP32. ggml has no CQ type, so CQ tensors are dequantized to F32 (exact in F32 arithmetic up to the Hadamard matmul rounding); FP16 tensors keep F16 storage and FP32 tensors stay F32 (Policy 2). Reference dtype label: F32.

reference_rationale: There is no first-party source implementation of Whistle's audio path. The only publisher-supported executable is the closed prebuilt Needle engine (Cactus-Compute/needle3 binaries / cactus-needle wheel) running whistle.cact. The user selected it as a black-box oracle on 2026-10-09 over (a) pausing for Cactus to publish code, (b) adopting the third-party mrfakename/whistle-ONNX PyTorch port, and (c) dropping the port; selecting it explicitly waives the CLAUDE.md 'do not guess' rule for the components with no source (mel frontend details, conv stem, encoder block, cross-attention, pe_gate, decode loop). The engine is authoritative for end-to-end transcripts, detected language, word times and the encoder embedding (needle_embed); first-party JAX code in cactus-compute/needle (architecture.py, export.py) is authoritative for the shared decoder blocks and the .cact/CQ format. No intermediate tensor dumps are available from the oracle, so Stage 2 dumps are limited to engine-observable outputs.
known_risks: Reference is a closed binary: no tensor dumps below the encoder output (needle_embed) and the final transcript/words; layer-by-layer bring-up has no oracle and must be validated end-to-end.

Do-not-guess waiver in effect: mel window/log/normalization/centering, conv stem wiring, encoder block order (attn + conv module + two Hadamard MLPs), cross-attention, pe_gate and the decode loop are reconstructed from tensor names, shapes and the experiments-branch prototype; each reconstruction must be confirmed against engine outputs.

Weights are the deployed CQ 2/4-bit .cact dequantized to F32, not the F32 QAT masters; dequantization (codebook * group L2 norm, then normalized Walsh-Hadamard over 128) must be bit-checked against needle/model/quantize.py and export.py.

Engine numerics are not F32: int8 KV cache (kv_bits=8 in the header) and 8-bit activations (act_bits=8) in QAT; an F32 ggml port will not be bit-exact and parity must be judged on transcripts/WER, not tensors.

Engine decodes with 5-beam search by default; transcribe.cpp has no beam search. Stage 2 must find out whether the engine can run greedy for a like-for-like baseline, else accept a greedy-vs-beam WER delta.

Hard input cap of 30 s per pass (max_audio_seconds=30; decoder max_tokens=320, max_seq_len=320). Long-form behavior beyond 30 s needs a chunking policy; the engine's own long-audio path is stream-based.
Decoder self-attention uses causal depthwise q/k/v taps (width 3) across decoded tokens: the KV cache must also carry the previous 2 pre-tap projections per layer.
mHC hyper-connections: 4 residual lanes with Sinkhorn-normalized lane-mixing matrices in both encoder and decoder; the Sinkhorn iteration count and whether it is precomputed must match the engine.

Engram hashed n-gram embeddings at decoder sites 3 and 7 (orders 2,3; 2 heads; 18432 slots; 4-tap dilated conv): hashing over the token history is host-side integer logic and must match exactly, including at the BOS/language-token boundary.

HadamardMLP is a structured Kronecker (16x16 x 32x32) Walsh-Hadamard MLP with fixed permutations (shipped as FP32 [512] vectors) and a rank-8 cond_u/cond_v correction; no direct ggml op, needs a custom decomposition.
Prompt/language semantics unknown: whether the decoder prompt is <s><|lang|> and how auto-LID scores the 7 language tokens (argmax at step 1 or restricted) is engine-internal.
Silence/steady noise must return empty text and empty language; the mechanism (no-speech threshold, EOS-first, energy gate) is undocumented.
Word timestamps come from DTW over decoder cross-attention; which layers/heads and the DTW normalization are undocumented.
Keyword biasing is a decode-time search bias with undocumented weights; it does not map 1:1 onto transcribe.cpp's prompt-based vocabulary feature.
Decoder depth ladder (--audio-depth N, N>=2) selects a layer subset per ladder_layer_indices(); the default depth the engine runs and benchmarks with must be confirmed (assumed full 8).
Engine-side streaming (needle_stream_transcribe_*) is a re-decode policy committing words that two passes agree on; the model itself is an offline 30 s window.

Acceptance set exceeds the cap: 9 of 2620 LibriSpeech test-clean utterances are longer than 30 s (max 34.95 s). The engine Oracle baseline and the C++ port must treat them identically (reject, truncate, or chunk), or the REF-vs-C++ WER gate compares different inputs.
The cactus-needle Python wrapper sends usage telemetry and re-fetches config.json from HF on every load; Stage 2 reference runs must set NEEDLE_TELEMETRY=0.

The cactus-needle wrapper caches weights and engines under ~/.cache/cactus-needle (outside the sandbox); Stage 2 must point NEEDLE_WHISTLE_WEIGHTS at the HF-cache whistle.cact and NEEDLE3_LIB_PATH at an engine under refs/ so nothing is written there.
